record.context_brief: Asymptotic growth of diagonal centerpole numbers
record.original_question: What is the growth rate of the sequence {c_r^0(R^r)}_{r=1}^∞? Is it exponential or polynomial in r?

evidence.quote: Observe that the upper bound for c0r(Rr) in Theorem 10.3 has exponential growth while the lower bound has polynomial growth.
Problem 10.8. What is the growth of the sequence (c0r(Rr))∞r=1? Exponential or polynomial?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a topological group $G$ and a positive integer $r$, a subset $C\subseteq G$ is called an $r$-centerpole if for every Borel $r$-coloring $\chi:G\to\{1,\dots,r\}$ there exist a color class $A=\chi^{-1}(i)$, an unbounded subset $S\subseteq A$, and a point $c\in C$ such that $S$ is centrally symmetric about $c$, i.e. $S=cS^{-1}c$ (equivalently, $s\in S\iff c\,s^{-1}c\in S$).

Consider $G=\mathbb{R}^r$ (with the usual topology and additive group structure) and its diagonal subgroup $\Delta_r=\{(t,t,\dots,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^r$. Define the diagonal centerpole number
$$c_r^{0}(\mathbb{R}^r)=\min\{\,|C|:C\subseteq\Delta_r\text{ is an }r\text{-centerpole in }\mathbb{R}^r\,\}.$$
It is known that $c_r^0(\mathbb{R}^r)$ admits a polynomial lower bound and an exponential upper bound in $r$.

Determine the asymptotic growth of the sequence $\bigl(c_r^{0}(\mathbb{R}^r)\bigr)_{r=1}^{\infty}$ as $r\to\infty$. In particular, decide whether this growth is polynomial or exponential in $r$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the asymptotic growth of the diagonal centerpole numbers c_r^0(R^r), where the known bounds are polynomial from below and exponential from above. Web searches reveal related work by Banakh and collaborators on centerpole sets for colorings of Abelian and topological groups, but no source has been located that closes this gap or determines the precise growth rate. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Centerpole sets for colorings of Abelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: A subset C of a topological group G is called k-centerpole if for each Borel k-coloring of G there is an unbounded monochromatic subset which is symmetric with respect to a point c in C.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the standard definition of centerpole sets used in defining c_r^0; does not resolve the growth of c_r^0(R^r).

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Symmetric monochromatic subsets in colorings — foundational treatment of symmetry/coloring invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Background on symmetric monochromatic subsets in colorings; does not address the precise growth rate question.
